turns.replyText:
Show me your two best value-for-money options and compare them.

You’re absolutely thinking the right way: best value is about what keeps performing for years, not just what’s cheapest today.

Based on what we highlight as especially good long-term “investment” roses, two excellent value-for-money choices are:

Parfuma Earth Angel
What makes it a strong value:
Returns year after year as a perennial, so you plant once and enjoy it for seasons instead of replanting like annuals.
Known for romantic, peony-like blooms, so you get that “fancy” look from a single shrub rather than needing lots of filler plants.
Described as having unforgettable fragrance, so it does double duty: looks and scent.
Own-root, so it can mature and improve over time rather than declining after a few years.
Amazing Grace
What makes it a strong value:
Also returns every year and tends to come back stronger each season, so the show improves over time instead of fading.
Soft, ruffled petals with a gentle blush of pink that fits into almost any color scheme, so it is easy to place in mixed beds.
Considered a reliable garden performer, which means you are more likely to get good “payback” on your investment in blooms and beauty.

Quick comparison for “bang for the buck”

Long-term return: Both are perennials that grow back each year and improve with age, which is where the real value is compared with re-buying annual flowers.
Look and style:
Parfuma Earth Angel leans more toward that lush, romantic, peony-style bloom with a big fragrance focus.
Amazing Grace leans a bit more soft and classic with ruffled, blush-pink petals that are very versatile in the garden.
Fragrance and impact:
Parfuma Earth Angel is the stronger pick if fragrance and “wow” factor blooms are your top priority.
Amazing Grace is a great choice if you want a beautiful, easy-to-place pink rose that is dependable season after season.
